items.name: account-deletion
items.title: Account deletion with a grace period
items.description: Self-service and admin account deletion for server apps: re-authenticated requests, a configurable grace period during which the account is disabled, cancel to restore access, session revocation through a hook, a declared delete/anonymize/retain data policy run by a leased, resumable, run-once worke
items.docs: Genlib module account-deletion@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlAccountDeletionStore with your query executor; on other databases implement AccountDeletionStore with one live (pending, executing or completed) request per user and conditional, lease-checked claim, renew, step, complete and release statements. Implement authorize(actor, 'request'|'cancel'|'read', {userId, self}) so owners (self) and the admins you choose are allowed. Pass revokeSessions(userId) that revokes every session, refresh token and API token of the user. Declare the data policy: one entry per data set with action delete, anonymize or retain, a reason, and an idempotent run(); put the account row itself last. Set graceMs (default 30 days) and recentAuthMs (default 5 minutes); give actors authenticatedAt from your sign-in or re-authentication step. Call isDisabled(userId) in sign-in and request authentication; for a disabled account offer only the cancel flow after verifying credentials. Call runDue({limit}) periodically from a scheduler or the durable-jobs module; set leaseMs longer than one policy step takes. Mount createAccountDeletionHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins and your authenticate(request). Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/account-deletion/CONTRACT.md

Optionally pass onAudit to write key.created, key.revoked, key.used and key.denied events to your audit log. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/api-keys/CONTRACT.md

items.description: Tenant-scoped, append-only audit log for multi-tenant apps: record who did what to which target, when, with what outcome and request id, in the same transaction as the change; per-tenant SHA-256 hash chain with tamper verification; redaction of secrets before hashing; admin-only filtered queries wit
items.docs: Genlib module audit-log@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, create the schema.sql objects as a dedicated owner role, then grant the application role only SELECT, INSERT on audit_log, SELECT on audit_log_heads and EXECUTE on audit_log_lock_head, and grant EXECUTE on audit_log_purge only to the retention job's role (see the header of schema.sql). Never give the application role UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, ALTER or ownership. Call audit.record(tx, entry) inside the same transaction as each security-relevant or data-changing action, passing that transaction's query executor; pass null to record on its own (failed logins, denied requests). Implement authorize(actor, 'read'|'export', {tenantId}) so only administrators of that tenant pass. Declare retentionMs (for example 365 days) and run audit.purgeExpired() from a scheduled job with the retention role. Optionally pass hmacKey (32+ random bytes from your secret store) so a database user cannot recompute hashes, and store audit.checkpoint(tenantId) outside the database periodically (and after each purge) to pass to verifyChain. Emails are masked by default (maskEmails: false keeps them); add your own sensitive keys with redactKeys and domain identifiers with redactPatterns. Mount createAuditLogHandler under one prefix with your authenticate(request). Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/audit-log/CONTRACT.md

items.name: bot-protection
items.title: Bot protection for forms
items.description: Stop signup, login and contact-form spam: server-side Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha and reCAPTCHA v2/v3 token checks (hostname, action, score, age, fail-closed), a privacy-friendly signed proof-of-work challenge with single-use replay protection, a honeypot with minimum fill time, one combined guar
items.docs: Genlib module bot-protection@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: Keep the captcha secret, the proof-of-work key and the honeypot key (each at least 32 bytes, different from each other) in your server secret store and pass them in; the module never reads the environment. Set expectedHostnames to the hosts that render the widget, expectedAction for Turnstile or reCAPTCHA v3, and minScore (default 0.5) for reCAPTCHA v3. Leave failOpen off unless an outage of the captcha provider must never block signups; with it on, bots pass during every outage. Create one guard per form with a server-chosen formId; mount createChallengeHandler with the same form ids and wrap each form's POST handler with protect(). Use MemoryReplayStore on a single server only; with several instances implement ReplayStore.consume atomically (Redis SET NX PX, a unique database key or a Durable Object). Pick maxNumber for your audience: about 20,000 Web Crypto hashes per second were measured in Node 22, so the default 50,000 averages about 1.3 s; run solveChallenge in a Web Worker. Pass clientIp only from a header your own proxy sets; never trust a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/bot-protection/CONTRACT.md

items.name: common-api-clients
items.title: Common API clients
items.description: Server-only TypeScript clients for GitHub, Stripe Checkout, Resend, Supabase reads, Microsoft Graph, Google Calendar, OpenAI, Anthropic, Saleor catalog reads, and Steel sessions with explicit credentials and bounded HTTP transport.
items.docs: Genlib module common-api-clients@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: Inject trusted token resolvers and Fetch configuration; never copy request headers, request JSON, user URLs, or client-supplied identity into client configuration. GitHub, Stripe, and Anthropic require an explicit supported API version; AI adapters also require a configured model and output token limit. Stripe requires approved server price mappings, return URLs, an order authorization callback, and a persisted idempotency key per attempt. Resend requires a verified server-owned sender, exact recipient/content authorization, and a persisted idempotency key per delivery event. Supabase requires a project HTTPS origin, publishable key, caller user token, and table/column allowlists; enable and test RLS in the target database. Graph requires a delegated Graph token; Calendar requires allowed calendar IDs and explicit time bounds; these clients do not obtain or refresh OAuth tokens. Model calls require a mandatory application authorization callback; check tenant, data disclosure, and budget before allowing each paid call. Saleor requires a trusted GraphQL endpoint; Steel requires explicit authority for each session operation and careful handling of server-only connection URLs. items.docs: Genlib module scheduled-tasks@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlSchedulerStore with your query executor; on other databases implement SchedulerStore with a unique (schedule_id, scheduled_for) key and single-statement conditional updates for materialize, claim, slot, heartbeat and finish, and a due-run query that returns at most one run per schedule. Register handlers by name in createScheduler({handlers}); saved schedules store only the name and JSON payload, never code. Give each process a unique instanceId and call tick() at least once per graceMs (default 60 s); a platform cron route that hits one instance per minute also works. Pick per schedule: timeZone (IANA, default UTC), overlap (skip, queue or allow), catchUp (none, latest or all with maxCatchUp), maxAttempts and retry delays, and a leaseMs above your handler's longest pause between heartbeats. Make handlers idempotent per (scheduleId, scheduledFor): a run whose worker crashes after committing effects is retried after its lease expires. Pass onFailure to alert when a run fails for good, and prune old rows from scheduled_task_runs on a schedule. items.name: security-headers
items.title: Security headers
items.description: Framework-neutral TypeScript builder for HTTP response security headers: validated Content-Security-Policy with per-request nonces and report-only mode, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, and X-Frame-Options, applied to Fetch Responses.
items.docs: Genlib module security-headers@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: csp merges per directive over default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'. A directive set to false is removed, true emits a valueless directive, and csp: false omits the header. nonce (from createNonce, generated per response) is appended to nonceDirectives (default script-src); the application must put the same nonce on its script tags. reportOnly sends Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only. hsts defaults to max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, preload is opt-in, and hsts: false omits it for plain-HTTP development. referrerPolicy, permissionsPolicy (merged over camera/microphone/geolocation/payment/usb/browsing-topics disabled), crossOriginOpenerPolicy, frameOptions, and contentTypeOptions can each be changed or disabled with false. withSecurityHeaders preserves existing response headers unless override: true. Invalid configuration throws a TypeError. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/security-headers/CONTRACT.md

items.name: short-links
items.title: Short links
items.description: URL shortener for multi-tenant apps: create short links with random or custom codes, validated destinations, expiry, disable and click limits, an atomic click counter, a redirect route and a management API, with injected authorization and persistence.
items.docs: Genlib module short-links@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlShortLinkStore with your query executor; on other databases implement ShortLinkStore with a unique code and a single conditional increment for recordClick. Implement authorize(actor, 'create'|'manage'|'read', {tenantId}) from your own membership table. Pass your own short domain (and app domain) in blockHosts so links cannot redirect to themselves. Optionally pass isSafeDestination to call a safe-browsing service from the trusted server. Mount createRedirectHandler on the short domain; mount createManagementHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins and your authenticate(request). Optionally pass onClick to store click events (link id, time, referrer host, country) in your analytics table; never add raw IPs. items.name: site-search
items.title: Site search with filters
items.description: Full-text search with filters for a multi-tenant app's own records (products, articles, tickets): weighted fields, a safe query syntax (words, phrases, -exclusions, prefix* type-ahead), keyword, range and boolean filters, facets, highlights, keyset paging and per-document visibility, with an in-memo
items.docs: Genlib module site-search@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlSearchStore(executor, { config: 'english' | 'simple' }); elsewhere implement SearchStore (upsert, remove, search) or use MemorySearchStore for small single-process datasets. Declare weighted text fields ({ title: 'A', body: 'C' }) and filterable attributes ({ category: 'keyword', price: 'number', publishedAt: 'date', inStock: 'boolean' }); keep the field order stable because the SQL store builds tsv in that order. Implement authorize(actor, action, tenantId) for search and index from your membership table; for search, return the actor's principals (groups, roles, user id) that document visibility lists are matched against. Index from your own write path (after a product, article or ticket is saved) and remove on delete; re-index everything after changing fields or weights. Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token, never from the request body. Mount createSearchHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/site-search/CONTRACT.md

items.name: soft-delete
items.title: Soft delete and restore
items.description: Soft delete, trash and restore layer for a multi-tenant app's own tables: deleted_at/deleted_by/delete_batch marks, cascade to declared child tables by batch id, restore within a retention window that reports unique conflicts, an idempotent purge job, PostgreSQL schema pattern with partial unique in
items.docs: Genlib module soft-delete@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: Add deleted_at (bigint epoch ms), deleted_by and delete_batch columns to each soft-deletable table, replace its unique constraints with partial unique indexes WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, and keep plain (NO ACTION) foreign keys; schema.sql shows the pattern and creates the soft_delete_batches trash table. Declare entities: table -> { unique: column sets unique among live rows of a tenant, children: [{ entity, foreignKey }] }. Point default reads (lists, search, counts, exports) at a live view (liveViewSql) or add liveCondition() to every query; optionally add a row-level security policy that hides deleted rows. Implement authorize(actor, 'delete'|'restore'|'trash'|'read', { tenantId, entity }) from your own membership table. Call softDelete.remove from your own delete routes; mount createTrashHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins and your authenticate(request). Run purgeExpired() from a trusted scheduler (for example the durable-jobs module) at least daily; set retentionMs (default 30 days) to your retention policy. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/soft-delete/CONTRACT.md

items.name: structured-logger
items.title: Structured logger
items.description: Framework-neutral TypeScript JSON-lines logger with levels, child bindings, deterministic key-based redaction, bounded cycle-safe serialization, error cause chains, an injectable sink and clock, and x-request-id correlation for Fetch Request objects.
items.docs: Genlib module structured-logger@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: createLogger({ level, sink, base, redact, includeStack, clock, maxDepth, maxStringLength, maxArrayLength, maxKeys, maxCauseDepth, maxLineBytes }); every option has a safe default. Pass the level from application configuration (for example an env-config field); the module does not read environment variables. Add application-specific sensitive field names through redact; they extend the default list. withRequest(logger, request, { header, trustIncoming, generate }) returns a child logger and requestId; set the same ID on the response. items.name: tenant-isolation
items.title: Tenant isolation
items.description: Multi-tenant data isolation for SaaS apps: resolve the tenant from the verified session and membership (client-sent ids are only selectors), PostgreSQL row-level security with transaction-local tenant settings and a non-bypass role, a tenant-scoped repository, and a reusable cross-tenant test kit.
items.docs: Genlib module tenant-isolation@0.1.1 (Apache-2.0). Configure: Apply schema.sql (or appRoleSql() and tenantTableSql('your_table') for each tenant table) as the database owner; every tenant table needs a tenant_id column leading its indexes. Run application queries as a role that is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS: log in as a member of app_user, or pass { role: 'app_user' } to withTenant and GRANT app_user to the login user. Supply session(request) from your verified session or token and memberships(userId) from your membership table; optionally a selector (headerSelector, pathSelector or subdomainSelector). On a connection pool, give the executor a transaction(work) that checks out one client for BEGIN ... COMMIT so set_config and SET LOCAL ROLE stay on that connection. Call assertTenantIsolation from your own test suite against each tenant table in a test database. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/tenant-isolation/CONTRACT.md

items.name: two-factor
items.title: Two-factor authentication with an authenticator app (TOTP)
items.description: TOTP two-factor authentication for server apps: 160-bit secrets with otpauth:// QR URIs, confirm-before-enable enrollment, RFC 6238 verification with a one-step window and replay protection, per-account attempt limits, AES-256-GCM secrets at rest with key rotation, HMAC-peppered one-time recovery co
items.docs: Genlib module two-factor@0.2.1 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlTwoFactorStore with your query executor; on other databases implement TwoFactorStore with single-statement conditional updates for activate, advanceStep, consumeRecoveryCode and registerAttempt. Generate a 32-byte AES key from a secret manager and pass it as encryption.keys[<id>] with currentKeyId; to rotate, add a new id, make it current, keep the old id until reencryptSecret has run for every user. Pass recoveryPepper: at least 32 random bytes from a secret manager, kept separate from the database. Set issuer to your product name (no colon); the account name is usually the user's email. After a password sign-in, check isEnabled(userId) and, when true, hold a second-factor-pending session until verify or verifyRecoveryCode succeeds. Pass authenticatedAt (when the user last proved their password) to disable and regenerateRecoveryCodes; re-prompt for the password when they refuse with reauthentication-required. For a lockout policy (N consecutive failures lock the account for a fixed time from the Nth) pass lockoutMs; for strict six-digit input pass allowCodeSpaces: false. Mount createTwoFactorHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins, an authenticate hook that reports the session stage, a rateLimit(key) hook, a trusted clientIp(request) and an onVerified hook that upgrades the session. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/two-factor/CONTRACT.md

items.name: url-slugs
items.title: URL slugs
items.description: Title-to-slug generation for server apps: Latin diacritic transliteration and optional Unicode scripts, word-boundary length cap, concurrency-safe unique slugs per tenant scope with numeric suffixes, reserved route words, rename history with 301 redirects that never chain or loop, a PostgreSQL store
items.docs: Genlib module url-slugs@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlSlugStore (table may be schema-qualified) with a query executor that also offers transaction() (needed for rename); elsewhere implement SlugStore with a unique (scope, slug) key and a unique current slug per (scope, entity). Build each scope with slugScope(tenantId, collection) from trusted server context, never from the URL or request body. Pass reserved: [...DEFAULT_RESERVED_SLUGS, ...yourRouteNames] so no slug can shadow a route; set maxLength, separator, unicode and fallback to match your URLs. Call create when the entity is created, rename when its title or slug changes and remove when it is deleted; store the returned slug on your entity if you need it in listings. Mount createSlugResolveHandler with routes, prefix and a scopeFor(request, params) that reads the tenant from the session or verified host, or call slugs.resolve from your page handler and issue the redirect yourself. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/url-slugs/CONTRACT.md

items.name: web-push
items.title: Web Push notifications
items.description: Send Web Push notifications from your server with Web Crypto only: RFC 8291 aes128gcm payload encryption, VAPID (RFC 8292) signing and key generation, per-user subscriptions with endpoint allow-list and dedupe, TTL/urgency/topic headers, cleanup of expired subscriptions on 404/410, bounded-concurren
items.docs: Genlib module web-push@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: Run generateVapidKeys() once, store the private key as a server secret and pass {publicKey, privateKey, subject} (a mailto: or https: contact) to createWebPush; rotating the keys invalidates every existing subscription. On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlPushSubscriptionStore with your query executor; on other databases implement PushSubscriptionStore keyed by endpoint with an atomic failure counter. Pass the platform fetch; keep the default push service host allow-list unless you serve browsers with other push services, then set allowedHosts or allowAnyHttpsEndpoint. Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token and mount createWebPushHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy. Put serviceWorkerSnippet in your service worker file and subscribe in the page with pushManager.subscribe({userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey}) using the key from GET {prefix}/vapid-public-key. Call send or sendMany from server jobs; retry rate-limited and server-error results after retryAfterSeconds with your queue. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/web-push/CONTRACT.md

items.name: webhook-delivery
items.title: Outgoing webhook delivery with retries
items.description: Send webhooks from a multi-tenant server app: tenant-scoped endpoint management behind an authorize hook, Standard Webhooks signatures with secret rotation, a durable delivery queue written on the caller's transaction, a leased worker with per-attempt timeouts, exponential backoff with jitter, dead-
items.docs: Genlib module webhook-delivery@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlWebhookStore with your query executor; elsewhere implement WebhookDeliveryStore with a unique (endpoint_id, event_id), an atomic leased claim, lease renewal and completion fenced by the lease owner. Pass fetch (globalThis.fetch, or a pinning fetch that connects only to context.addresses), resolveHost (for example node:dns/promises lookup with {all: true}) and authorize(actor, tenantId, action) backed by your membership and role checks. Call enqueue({tenantId, eventId, type, data}, {tx}) with an executor bound to the transaction that makes the business change; use a stable eventId per business event. Run runOnce({workerId}) on a schedule with a unique workerId per process; keep leaseMs at least max(timeoutMs x ceil(limit / concurrency), timeoutMs + 1 s); each attempt renews the lease when it starts. Optionally pass a secretBox to encrypt stored secrets with your key management service. Mount createWebhookEndpointsHandler under one prefix with authenticate(request) from your session layer and exact allowedOrigins. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/webhook-delivery/CONTRACT.md

items.name: webhook-verification
items.title: Webhook verification
items.description: Framework-neutral TypeScript verification of inbound webhook HMAC-SHA256 signatures over raw body bytes with Web Crypto: generic hex, GitHub, Stripe, and Standard Webhooks/Svix, with secret rotation, timestamp tolerance, and a size-capped raw body reader.
items.docs: Genlib module webhook-verification@0.1.0 (Apache-2.0). Configure: Supply each signing secret from trusted server configuration; pass an array (1-10, current first) during rotation. String secrets are UTF-8 key bytes except Standard Webhooks, which expects whsec_<base64> (16-128 decoded bytes). Stripe and Standard Webhooks accept toleranceSeconds (default 300, 1-86400, enforced in both directions) and an injectable clock returning epoch milliseconds. readRawBody(request, maxBytes) requires an explicit cap from 1 byte to 64 MiB; choose the provider's documented maximum payload size. Invalid configuration (missing/oversized secrets, bad tolerance, bad cap) throws a TypeError with a fixed message that never contains secret material; request input never throws. Contract: https://github.com/athompson83/genlib/blob/main/modules/webhook-verification/CONTRACT.md
